chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ma'bad or someone else, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For the hearts there is a welcoming (inclination) and a turning back (aversion). So whenever it inclines, perform optional prayers, and whenever it turns back, stick to the obligatory prayers.'

key_terms.إِدْبَار: Spiritual aversion or turning away of the heart
key_terms.إِقْبَال: Spiritual inclination or receptivity of the heart

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do with their prayers when they feel spiritually distracted or dry?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the dynamic nature of spiritual states, advising believers to capitalize on moments of heightened receptivity (iqbal) for voluntary (nawafil) prayers while anchoring themselves in obligatory (fard) duties during periods of spiritual dryness or distraction (idbar). Scholars emphasize this as a practical strategy for maintaining consistent worship, ensuring that the foundation of faith remains intact even when the heart's inclination wanes.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, or someone else,

(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws having said: ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘For the hearts there is a welcoming and a turning back. So whenever it welcomes, so you tend to pray optional (Salāt), and when it turns back, so upon you is with the Obligatory (Salāts)’.
en.sarwar: 16. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by ibn Ma’bad or someone other than him who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said that the Holy prophet has said, ‘
Hearts work with interest or with abhorrence. When they are interested, perform optional Salah (prayer) but when they have abhorrence then hold to obligatory Salah (prayer).’”
